personality_one_liner: A highly operational, rugged, and clipboard-like command center designed for occupied hands and fast tracking in busy professional kitchens.

spacing.rule: Use rigid grids, exposed structure, and deliberate visual tension. Hard alignment and oversized typography. Elements should be extremely easy to tap for kitchen staff with occupied or messy hands.

do's: Use solid surfaces and hard 1-2pt borders to separate sections.
dont's: No blur, no translucency, no soft gradients. The interface must be completely opaque and high-contrast.

screens.name: Dashboard (Home)
screens.purpose: A command-center view highlighting today's critical tasks, expiring batches, and giant action buttons for fast data entry.

states.loading: High-contrast skeleton blocks locking the grid in place.
states.empty: No active tasks? Show a large 'All Clear' success state with a massive scanner CTA.
states.error: Bold red container stating connection issues with a hard-edged 'Retry' button.

screens.layout: Grid-based modular layout. Top section: Day's summary and alerts in a sharp, contrasting box. Middle section: A 2-column grid of oversized action buttons (New Reception, Temperatures, Cleaning, etc.) with large Phosphor icons and 2pt borderStrong outlines. Bottom/FAB: A massive, sticky scanner button that cannot be missed.

screens.name: Product Reception Form
screens.purpose: Fast, step-by-step data logging for incoming goods with photo proof capability.

states.error: Inline red validation text under missed inputs, thick red border on the field.

screens.layout: Single column, edge-to-edge input fields separated by thick horizontal dividers. Labels sit above inputs using Space Grotesk. Massive 'Add Photo' regions that open the camera directly. The 'Save Reception' CTA must be pinned to the bottom (KeyboardAvoidingView) and span 100% width.

screens.name: Scanner
screens.purpose: High-speed barcode and QR code ingestion.

states.error: Invalid code alert with manual entry fallback.

screens.layout: Full-screen camera viewfinder with a high-contrast targeting reticle. When a code is detected, a bottom sheet instantly snaps up with the product details, allowing one-tap logging of temperature or status.

screens.name: Batch Traceability
screens.purpose: Detailed historical timeline of a product's lifecycle from reception to plate.
screens.layout: A rigid, vertical timeline. Left column: Dates/Times in JetBrains Mono. Right column: Event blocks (Reception, Temp Check, Cleaning) in high-contrast solid containers. No soft curves—everything is bracketed and industrial.

screens.name: Temperature Control
screens.purpose: Quick logging of daily temperatures for all storage units.
screens.layout: List of large rectangular cards for each unit (Cold Room, Freezer, Display). Each card has an integrated numeric keypad or massive +/- steppers to input temps without opening the keyboard. Semantic color-coding: green background if within limits, orange/red if non-conforming.

instructions_to_main_agent: Follow the Brutalist personality strictly: 0 radius everywhere, 1-2pt hard borders (borderStrong), and absolutely no shadows or glassmorphism.
Do not use blue anywhere in the app. Use the defined Industrial Orange (#E65100) for primary actions.
Implement massive touch targets (min 56pt) for all buttons and list items, considering the primary user will be in a kitchen with occupied or messy hands.
Semantic colors (Green/Yellow/Red) should be used aggressively to signify compliance vs. non-compliance in lists and timelines.
Include the images provided for empty states, onboarding, or category headers using the required gradient-to-dark scrim pattern to ensure text legibility.
Make the Scanner functionality extremely prominent, either as a massive FAB or the center tab bar item.
The app must be translated/built in French as per the problem statement.
